title: That’s an Order!
bodyHtml:
Cebuano is an Austronesian language spoken in the Philippines. The language was heavily influenced by Spanish during a period of colonialism from 1521 to 1898.

Your task is to figure out what four women, Althea, Inday, Janelle, and Maria, had for lunch. Each person had a main dish as well as a dessert and a drink. No two people ordered the same main dish, no two people ordered the same dessert, and no two people ordered the same drink.

Each of them chose from the following Philippine menu:

Main Dishes

adobong baboy
Pork dish cooked in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.
adobong sitaw
String beans cooked in the adobo style (with soy sauce and vinegar).
asado
Beef dish cooked in a sauce with tomatoes, olives, onion, ketchup, red bell pepper, and potatoes.
bulanglang
Boiled mixed vegetables, including malunggay leaves, squash and onions in rice washing.

Desserts

buko pie
A traditional Filipino baked young coconut custard pie.
kutsinta
A type of steamed rice cake made with rice flour, brown sugar and lye.
maruya
Banana fritters, served in syrup or ice cream.
turon saba
Deep fried plantains in spring roll wrappers.

Drinks

bino
Wine.
gatas
Milk.
serbesa
Beer.
tubig
Water.

D1. Based on the following clues try to determine who ordered which food and drink. Write your answers in Cebuano.

  • Janelle nikaon og bulanglang apan dili og turon saba.
  • Ang tao nga nipalit og asado ug nikaon og kutsinta wala niinom og serbesa.
  • Ang tao nga nikaon og adobong baboy ug niinom og tubig apan si dili Althea.
  • Ang duha ka tao nga nanginon alkohol mga Maria ug ang tao nga nipalit og adobong sitaw.
  • Inday nipalit og maruya.
  • Ang tolo ka tao nga wala nipalit og maruya mga Maria, Althea, ug Janelle.
  • Ang tao nga nikaon og bulanglang si Janelle.
  • Janelle nipalit og bulanglang apan dili og tubig.
AltheaIndayJanelleMaria
Main Dish
Dessert
Drink

questions.partPrompt: Based on the following clues try to determine who ordered which food and drink. Write your answers in Cebuano.

hints.text: The menu already gives you every food and drink word, so the only unknown words in the clues are the grammar words: nikaon, nipalit, niinom, apan, dili, wala, ug, ang tao nga, si, mga, duha, tolo. Work out what each of those does before you touch the grid.

Two words in the clues do the work of English "not": dili and wala. Two others count people: duha ka tao and tolo ka tao. And "ang tao nga ..." builds a phrase meaning "the person who ...", which lets a clue describe someone by their order instead of naming them. Once the clues are in English, treat it as an ordinary logic grid: three tables (person by main dish, person by dessert, person by drink) plus links between them.

Try the line "Ang tao nga nipalit og asado ug nikaon og kutsinta wala niinom og serbesa." Piece by piece: "ang tao nga" is "the person who", "nipalit og" is "bought", "ug" joins a second verb phrase "nikaon og" = "ate", and "wala niinom og" is "did not drink". So that single sentence links one main dish to one dessert and rules one drink out for that same person - three grid facts from one line. Do the same for every line before you start crossing cells out.

explanationHtml:
Step 1: crack the grammar words

Every food and drink name is already given to you in the menu, so the only things you have to figure out are the little words that hold the clues together. Compare these two lines:

  • Janelle nikaon og bulanglang apan dili og turon saba.
  • Janelle nipalit og bulanglang apan dili og tubig.

They are built the same way, with different verbs. nikaon shows up before food, niinom shows up before drinks, and nipalit shows up before both - so they mean "ate", "drank" and "bought". og is a little marker in front of the thing eaten, drunk or bought, and apan is "but".

Negation comes in two shapes: dili negates a noun or a name ("not turon saba", "not Althea"), while wala negates a verb ("did not drink", "did not buy").

Ang tao nga ... means "the person who ...": it lets a clue point at someone by their order rather than by name. si introduces a personal name ("was Janelle"), and mga introduces a list of names. Finally duha ka tao is "two people" and tolo ka tao is "three people", and ug is "and"/"also".

Step 2: the clues in English

  1. Janelle ate bulanglang but not turon saba.
  2. The person who bought asado also ate kutsinta but didn't drink beer (serbesa).
  3. The person who ate adobong baboy also drank tubig but was not Althea.
  4. The two people who had alcohol were Maria and the person who bought adobong sitaw.
  5. Inday bought maruya.
  6. The three people who did not buy maruya were Maria, Althea, and Janelle.
  7. The person who ate bulanglang was Janelle.
  8. Janelle bought bulanglang but not tubig.

Note that the two alcoholic drinks on the menu are bino (wine) and serbesa (beer); gatas (milk) and tubig (water) are not.

Step 3: work the grid

Clues 1, 7 and 8 all agree that Janelle's main dish is bulanglang, and clues 5 and 6 agree that Inday's dessert is maruya - so Janelle's dessert is not maruya, and clue 1 says it is not turon saba either. Clue 2 ties asado and kutsinta to the same person, and Janelle has bulanglang, so Janelle did not have kutsinta. Only one dessert is left for her.

Now for adobong baboy. Clue 3 rules out Althea, and Janelle already has bulanglang. Clue 4 says Maria drank alcohol, but clue 3 says the adobong baboy eater drank water, so Maria is out too. That pins adobong baboy on Inday, and gives Inday water at the same time.

Adobong sitaw and asado are left for Althea and Maria. Clue 4 lists Maria and the adobong sitaw buyer as two different people, so Maria did not buy adobong sitaw - she had asado, and Althea had adobong sitaw. Clue 2 then hands Maria the kutsinta, leaving turon saba for Althea.

Drinks finish themselves. By clue 4 the two alcohol drinkers are Maria and the adobong sitaw buyer, which is Althea. Clue 2 says the asado eater (Maria) did not drink beer, so Maria took wine and Althea took beer. Inday already has water, so Janelle gets the milk.

The finished order

AltheaIndayJanelleMaria
Main Dishadobong sitawadobong baboybulanglangasado
Dessertturon sabamaruyabuko piekutsinta
Drinkserbesatubiggatasbino

As a side note, the Spanish influence mentioned in the introduction is visible in the vocabulary itself: asado, serbesa (from cerveza), bino (from vino) and alkohol are all Spanish borrowings.
_reviewNotes: Answer keys taken verbatim from the official solution grid (Althea/Inday/Janelle/Maria columns; Main Dish, Dessert, Drink rows). The booklet itself prints no answer grid on the problem page (answers go on separate Answer Sheets); the 3x4 blank table in bodyHtml was reconstructed to match the solution grid's layout, so blank order is Main Dish row left to right (D1.1-D1.4), then Dessert (D1.5-D1.8), then Drink (D1.9-D1.12). No official per-part point breakdown was printed, so the 15 points are split evenly (1.25 per cell). No figures to crop.
